newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan opposition politician wins by-election.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan opposition politician wins by-election.

text.p: Kenyan opposition politician Raila Odinga retained his Nairobi parliament seat on Wednesday despite a turnout of less than seven percent of registered voters.
A spokesman for the National Electoral Commission (NEC) said Odinga received 4,798 votes compared with 1,844 for Fred Amayo, candidate of the ruling Kenya African National Union party.
Odinga, an outspoken opposition leader, is expected to be a presidential candidate in general elections due this year.

Partly because of deep rifts in the opposition, analysts expect President Daniel arap Moi, 72 and head of state since 1978, to be re-elected for a final five-year term under current constitutional rules.
But social tensions are running high with the government admitting serious poverty and Kenya regularly pilloried abroad for its abuse of human rights and rampant official corruption.
Only 7,060 voters or 6.8 percent of the registered voters cast their votes in Tuesday's by-election in Nairobi's Langata district, which includes some of the capital's poorest slums.

"We are satisfied the election was relatively free and fair," the NEC spokesman said. More than 70 people were arrested on Tuesday by police in Langata district, accused of possessing offensive weapons including clubs, whips and petrol bombs.
The by-election followed Odinga's resignation in December from the main opposition FORD-Kenya party after a leadership row. He then joined the little-known National Development Party.
